A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same continuous speculative decoding work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAR speedup, acceptance-rate, FID/IS, ablation, and qualitative results, including additional experiments in its supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains original MAR results and adds xAR and Harmon speed measurements, DDIM experiments, runtime measurements, and masked-generation results.

M1.justification: The acceptance rule, shared-noise trajectory alignment, token pre-filling, rejection sampling, and Algorithm 1 remain equivalent. v2 emphasizes avoiding repeated diffusion inference, but its rejection threshold and Gaussian sampling procedure already appear in v1 Equation 11 and Algorithm 1. Additional host models and sampler configurations do not establish a changed decoding algorithm.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from ImageNet 256 × 256 unconditional/class-conditioned generation to Harmon text-to-image generation at both 256 × 256 and 512 × 512 resolutions. xAR adds another model on the retained ImageNet task. GMM, audio, and video applications are discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix G.5 and Table 8 add MAR-H masked generation as an alternative acceleration comparator, evaluated across six masking configurations. The original vanilla-model and pure-draft comparisons remain. xAR and Harmon are additional host models, not competing decoding methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds xAR-B/H and Harmon-0.5B/1.5B configurations, uses xAR's tokenwise k=1 setting, and evaluates Harmon with smaller batches because of memory limits. New protocols include 100-step DDIM at batch size 256, rejection-sampling timing at batch size 1, and masked-generation sweeps. Alignment evaluation adds token distance, while speedup and ablation tables narrow the retained MAR model-pair sweep.

E4.justification: v2 adds alignment-distance measurements, DDIM testing, a rejection-sampling runtime breakdown, and masked-generation speed/quality analysis. It removes the visual alignment and pre-filling ablations in v1 Figures 10 and 12 and reduces their model-pair sweeps. Existing CFG, temperature, rejection-count, and acceptance-heatmap analyses are retained through relocation or consolidation.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.2 explicitly identifies the reported uncertainty as standard deviation; v1 presents the same ± values without identifying their type. Both appendices already specify ten evaluation runs, and the shared uncertainty values are unchanged. There is no documented increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Shared MAR-H/MAR-B speedups and MAR FID/IS entries remain unchanged. v2 newly reports up to 2.72× for xAR, 2.54× for Harmon at 512 resolution, and 2.30× for MAR with DDIM, alongside token-distance, runtime, and masking results. These are additional experimental settings, not same-setting MAR improvements. Speedup and ablation rows involving MAR-L are removed.

T1.justification: v2 introduces Theorem 1 and a substantial Appendix A.1 proof quantifying the expected squared-distance reduction from shared Gaussian noise. This mathematical result is absent from v1. The distribution-preservation proof is retained, while Corollary 1 largely formalizes the rejection-threshold derivation already present in v1.

C1.justification: The central claim of training-free, distribution-preserving continuous speculative decoding remains. v2 broadens the headline empirical claim from MAR acceleration up to 2.33× to over 2× across three model families and two resolutions. It also elevates alignment's avoidance of repeated diffusion inference into an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of applicability to explicit continuous PDFs, GMMs, alternative diffusion samplers, and untested audio/video domains. It expands explanations of alignment, rejection-sampling cost, and masking's speed/quality tradeoff. Its limitations discussion adds a batch-size explanation but drops v1's short-generation limitation; interpretations accompanying the removed visual ablations also disappear.

D1.justification: v2 reports code as available rather than forthcoming and documents additional model-specific details, including xAR's k=1 configuration and Harmon's separate text embeddings and memory-limited batches. The A100 hardware, official checkpoints, and 50,000-image MAR evaluation remain documented. v1's explicit statement that temperature and CFG follow MAR defaults is omitted, without establishing an actual setting change.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion involving xAR, Harmon, DiCoDe, DDIM, and LANTERN++, while trimming works such as FLUID, DART, RAR, Medusa, and BiLD. The central positioning against discrete speculative decoding remains intact. Publication updates for retained references do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and methodology are extensively rewritten. The method narrative changes from question-based subsections to continuous formulation, inconsistency mitigation, and resampling. The supplement is reorganized into separate algorithm, limitations, implementation, applicability, disclosure, and experiment sections, with some main-text analysis moved into it.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, redraws Figure 2, restructures speedup and ablation tables, and adds several experimental tables. Existing analyses are consolidated into v2 Figure 10, while two visual ablations are removed. The final qualitative galleries are retained with identical image content despite renumbering and resizing.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially broadens v1's single-model validation through xAR, Harmon, higher-resolution, and DDIM experiments. The alignment theorem and distance measurements, direct rejection-sampling timings, and masked-generation comparison strengthen the explanation and evidence for practical efficiency. These gains outweigh the narrower MAR ablation coverage, although image-quality validation remains limited to MAR and does not establish preservation on the newly evaluated models.
